title: King parties, stag parties and playing for the mayor
summary: He explains the king cake custom and recalls playing as boys for private parties and stags, picked up by the mayor's son.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: So, you mentioned some kind of king party or something?

Yeah, it's some custom they have here. And it might be elsewhere, but as I know it, it's in New Orleans. It's a party that the kids have. You know, they buy these cakes at the bakeries. And there's a little doll. Some kind of little china doll thing in the cake, baked in the cake. And then they slice the cake up and whoever finds that, either in his hand or in his mouth, is obligated to give the next party. You know, provide the refreshments and entertainment and the sight.
Oh. He's deaf, you know. Oh yeah. Oh, I see.
Well now, what were the other kind of parties you mentioned? And what did they consist of? What kind of customs?

Well, I think a lot of those parties were little private parties, just things that people gave just for the fun of it, you know. And I can remember also playing for the mayor of the city. And we were so small. In those days, the little boys wore short pants, not like today. As soon as they can walk around, they'd give them a pair of long pants. We had long black stockings and little short pants. And we couldn't get around because we had no transportation. And my mother wouldn't let us go out and play unless whoever hired us to play would agree to come and pick us up and bring us back home. Because there was no such thing as little boys roaming the streets at 12 and 1 o'clock in the morning, you know. And Mr. O'Keefe, the mayor, would send his son to my house. And they would pick us up and take us to wherever this party would be in and bring us back after. And in those days, the parties they gave were mainly stags. And not like we know stags today. In those days, we were just eating and drinking. That's all. A bunch of men, no entertainment other than a little musical aggregation. And then the main course, the spaghetti and the wine, the chicken and what have you.
